ROLE: Frame every complete packet currently buffered in a session's receive buffer, dispatch it to the matching protocol handler, consume exactly its bytes and stop at the first incomplete frame, the first malformed frame or a packet that closes the connection.

STRUCT.NAME: struct broker
STRUCT.ROLE: registry passed to the handlers; the private registry definition allows direct access to the slot array

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: connection whose receive buffer holds the stream bytes and whose state selects the permitted packets

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: session receive buffer; bytes of each handled packet are consumed from it

STRUCT.NAME: struct wire_header
STRUCT.ROLE: frame description: type, flags, remaining_length, header_len and total_len

FUNC.NAME: session_input
FUNC.ROLE: borrow the receive buffer to frame from

FUNC.NAME: session_state
FUNC.ROLE: select the packet set permitted by the connection state

FUNC.NAME: session_close_immediately
FUNC.ROLE: close on an invalid frame, a second CONNECT or a packet before CONNECT

FUNC.NAME: wire_decode_header
FUNC.ROLE: frame one packet and report WIRE_INCOMPLETE / WIRE_COMPLETE / WIRE_INVALID

FUNC.NAME: wire_decode_subscribe
FUNC.ROLE: decode and validate the SUBSCRIBE body

FUNC.NAME: wire_decode_publish
FUNC.ROLE: decode the PUBLISH topic, payload and flags

FUNC.NAME: wire_decode_empty
FUNC.ROLE: validate the PINGREQ/DISCONNECT fixed header and zero Remaining Length

FUNC.NAME: buffer_consume
FUNC.ROLE: drop the handled frame's bytes from the receive buffer

FUNC.NAME: handle_subscribe
FUNC.ROLE: same-file: store filters and queue SUBACK

FUNC.NAME: handle_publish
FUNC.ROLE: same-file: fan out a QoS 0 PUBLISH

VAR.NAME: WIRE_INCOMPLETE
VAR.ROLE: framing outcome that ends the loop with the partial bytes kept

VAR.NAME: WIRE_INVALID
VAR.ROLE: framing or decoding outcome that closes the connection

VAR.NAME: WIRE_PACKET_CONNECT
VAR.ROLE: type 1, the only packet allowed before CONNECT

VAR.NAME: SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT
VAR.ROLE: state in which only CONNECT is accepted

VAR.NAME: SESSION_READY
VAR.ROLE: state in which SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH/PINGREQ/DISCONNECT are accepted

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSED
VAR.ROLE: state reported to the caller as -1

VAR.NAME: BROKER_CLOSE
VAR.ROLE: handler outcome that stops processing and reports -1

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: wire_decode_header
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: enum wire_status wire_decode_header(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len, struct wire_header *out)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: WIRE_INCOMPLETE while fewer than total_len bytes are buffered (the Remaining Length field itself may be unfinished), WIRE_COMPLETE once len >= total_len, WIRE_INVALID for a reserved type (0, 15) or a Remaining Length field longer than 4 bytes; on COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE *out is filled with type, flags, remaining_length, header_len (2..5) and total_len = header_len + remaining_length, on INVALID *out is untouched
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: buf is borrowed and never modified; *out is caller storage
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: WIRE_INVALID leaves *out indeterminate, so the caller must not read a frame length from it: it closes the session instead

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: wire_decode_connect
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: enum wire_status wire_decode_connect(const uint8_t *packet, size_t len, struct wire_connect *out)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: WIRE_COMPLETE for a structurally valid CONNECT whose slices are filled (client_id, protocol_level, clean_session, keep_alive, has_will, has_user_name, has_password) or WIRE_INVALID for a malformed one; len must be the whole frame (header_len + remaining_length)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: all reported fields are borrowed slices into the packet the caller still owns
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: WIRE_INVALID means the CONNECT is malformed and the connection must be closed without a CONNACK

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: wire_decode_subscribe
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: enum wire_status wire_decode_subscribe(const uint8_t *packet, size_t len, struct wire_subscribe *out)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: WIRE_COMPLETE with the nonzero packet_id and the borrowed filter/QoS payload or WIRE_INVALID for flags != 0x2, packet id 0, an empty payload, an illegal filter or an illegal QoS byte
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: payload points into the packet, which the caller keeps alive until the frame is consumed
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: WIRE_INVALID closes the connection with no SUBACK

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: wire_decode_publish
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: enum wire_status wire_decode_publish(const uint8_t *packet, size_t len, struct wire_publish *out)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: WIRE_COMPLETE with topic/payload slices and qos/dup/retain, or WIRE_INVALID for an illegal topic name, QoS 3, DUP with QoS 0, or a missing/present-but-forbidden packet identifier
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: topic and payload point into the packet and are not copied here

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: wire_decode_empty
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: enum wire_status wire_decode_empty(const uint8_t *packet, size_t len, uint8_t expect_type, size_t *consumed)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: WIRE_COMPLETE with *consumed = 2 when the packet is exactly the 2 fixed-header bytes of type expect_type with flags 0 and Remaining Length 0; WIRE_INVALID otherwise
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: no bytes are retained; *consumed reports the frame size
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: WIRE_INVALID closes the connection (a nonzero Remaining Length on PINGREQ/DISCONNECT is a protocol violation)

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_consume
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; n bytes are removed from the front by moving the tail down and len is reduced by n
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: storage stays owned by the buffer, so a frame that was framed earlier stays intact only until this call returns
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; passing total_len consumes exactly the handled frame and preserves the following coalesced frames

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_input
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: borrowed pointer to the receive buffer (data/len/cap), NULL for a NULL session
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed; the session's reads and destroys keep the buffer alive, and this function never frees or replaces it, so in->data stays valid for the whole call

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_state
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the current lifecycle state; SESSION_CLOSED for NULL

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_close_immediately
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; queued output is released, the descriptor is closed once and the state becomes SESSION_CLOSED
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases the session's descriptor and queued bytes, but keeps the receive buffer so slices used by the current frame stay valid; the session object is freed later by broker_reap
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a no-op on an already CLOSED session

LOGIC.INPUT: b: broker registry handed to the handlers. s: the session whose receive buffer was filled by the execution layer; its state is SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT before its first CONNECT and SESSION_READY afterwards.
LOGIC.ACTION: in = session_input(s); if in is NULL or b is NULL, close s and return -1. Then repeat: (a) st = wire_decode_header(in->data, in->len, &h). If st == WIRE_INCOMPLETE return 0: fewer bytes than the whole packet are buffered (or the Remaining Length field itself is unfinished), the partial frame stays buffered for the next read, and no handler is invoked. If st == WIRE_INVALID (reserved type 0/15 or a Remaining Length field longer than 4 bytes) close the session and return -1. (b) The frame occupies exactly h.total_len bytes = h.header_len + h.remaining_length, which is <= in->len because the header decode reported WIRE_COMPLETE. (c) Dispatch by state: if session_state(s) == SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT, only h.type == WIRE_PACKET_CONNECT is legal; for any other type (including SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, PINGREQ, DISCONNECT and every server-only type) close the session immediately without a response and return -1, because CONNECT must be the first packet. For CONNECT decode with wire_decode_connect(in->data, h.total_len, &connect); a non-COMPLETE result closes the session and returns -1 (malformed CONNECT, no CONNACK); otherwise r = handle_connect(b, s, &connect). If session_state(s) == SESSION_READY, dispatch on h.type: WIRE_PACKET_SUBSCRIBE -> wire_decode_subscribe(in->data, h.total_len, &sub), r = handle_subscribe; WIRE_PACKET_PUBLISH -> wire_decode_publish(in->data, h.total_len, &pub), r = handle_publish; WIRE_PACKET_PINGREQ -> wire_decode_empty(in->data, h.total_len, WIRE_PACKET_PINGREQ, &consumed), r = handle_pingreq; WIRE_PACKET_DISCONNECT -> wire_decode_empty(in->data, h.total_len, WIRE_PACKET_DISCONNECT, &consumed), r = handle_disconnect; WIRE_PACKET_CONNECT (a second CONNECT on the same connection) closes the session immediately and returns -1; every other type (CONNACK, PUBACK/PUBREC/PUBREL/PUBCOMP, SUBACK, UNSUBSCRIBE/UNSUBACK, PINGRESP) is not accepted from a client by this broker and closes the session immediately without a response. A decoder result other than WIRE_COMPLETE closes the session and returns -1 before any handler runs, so no partially valid packet is ever acted upon. If session_state(s) is neither AWAITING_CONNECT nor READY (CLOSING or CLOSED) return -1 without consuming bytes: a session whose queue is draining must not process further input. (d) buffer_consume(in, h.total_len) drops exactly the handled frame, so the immediately following coalesced frame becomes the new head; the borrowed slices of the handled packet (client id, filters, topic, payload) are copied into session-owned storage by the handlers before this point, so no slice is used after the memmove. (e) If r == BROKER_CLOSE return -1 (the handler closed the session). Otherwise continue at (a) with the next frame. The loop is bounded by the buffered bytes, since every iteration either consumes a whole frame or returns.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: 0 when every complete frame was handled and either the buffer is empty or it holds only an incomplete trailing frame (those bytes stay buffered); -1 when the session was closed as a result of its input - an invalid frame, a second CONNECT, a non-CONNECT packet before CONNECT, an unsupported server-only packet type, a malformed packet body, or a handler that closed the session (CONNECT rejection, unsupported QoS, DISCONNECT). The function never reaps the registry itself, so the borrowed session pointer stays valid for the caller and the execution layer decides when to call broker_reap.
INVARIANTS_USED: only wire_decode_header reports WIRE_INCOMPLETE; every other decoder sees one complete frame
the bytes consumed for a handled packet are exactly header_len + remaining_length, so coalesced frames are handled in order and never overlap
CONNECT is the first packet of a connection and is accepted exactly once per connection
malformed input closes only the offending connection; the broker continues serving other sessions
handler-visible slices are borrowed from the receive buffer and are copied before the frame is consumed
a CLOSING session processes no further input, so a rejected client cannot keep sending
no session state is inherited by a later connection
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: b and s are non-NULL and s is owned by b; the receive buffer holds stream bytes appended by the execution layer (possibly a partial frame).
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: either s may continue (0, all complete frames handled, incomplete tail preserved and in->len < the size of one full frame) or s is SESSION_CLOSED and the return value is -1; in both cases b's registry count is unchanged because reaping is deferred to the caller.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Single-threaded reactor; the session and registry are not accessed concurrently.
